evidence: src/infrastructure/app.ts: createApp() is the only place that builds the repositories, UuidIdGenerator, use cases and controllers, and it registers every route through asyncHandler.
src/infrastructure/error-middleware.ts: errorMiddleware is the only place that maps ValidationError/NotFoundError/ConflictError to 400/404/409.

src/infrastructure/in-memory-*-repository.ts: each class implements its domain port (ProjectRepository, TaskRepository, UserRepository); the TaskFilter logic is only in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject.

src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts uses toTaskResponse from application/dtos; user-controller.ts and project-controller.ts build { id, name } inline. This is a minor inconsistency, and nothing shows a shared mapper they skip.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The 11 files form one coherent adapter layer for a single Task API. They group into four kinds of adapter: persistence (the three InMemory*Repository classes implementing the domain repository ports), ID generation (UuidIdGenerator implementing IdGenerator), HTTP (the three controllers, asyncHandler and errorMiddleware) and a composition root (createApp in app.ts, which server.ts only starts). The folder mixes HTTP delivery and persistence, but I don't count that as a split into unrelated concerns: both are adapters for the same application and meet in one composition root. Rules are kept in one place. The HTTP status mapping for domain errors lives only in errorMiddleware. Async error forwarding lives only in asyncHandler, and every route uses it. The task filter logic is only in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject. The repeated Map-based save/findById in the three repositories is a small, repeated pattern, not a business rule. One weak signal: TaskController uses toTaskResponse from application/dtos, while UserController and ProjectController build { id, name } inline. I can't call this a bypass because nothing shows that dtos.ts has a user or project mapper. If it does, this should become a violation.
